description: Where a participant is looking and what their face is doing. Included because gaze direction is one of the highest-frequency descriptors in the folksonomies that open adult models were trained on, and because it is the axis with the largest effect on how a still reads while costing the least to control. Per-participant, not per-pose. Adults only.

design_notes.why_gaze_is_separate_from_affect: Gaze target and facial affect vary independently: eye contact with a neutral face and eye contact with an open-mouthed expression are different images. Folksonomy tags bundle them; separating them makes both controllable.
design_notes.consent_signalling: Gaze and affect together carry most of the consent signal a viewer reads from an image. Values that read as distress are enumerated and flagged rather than omitted, so that a consumer can exclude them by rule instead of by absence.

dimensions.scale_citation: Direction-of-look descriptor; the highest-frequency single descriptor across booru-style adult folksonomies.

values.definition: Direct eye contact with the lens.
values.mechanical_gloss: looking directly into the camera lens

values.definition: Head turned back toward the lens or partner behind. Characteristic of from-behind arrangements.
values.mechanical_gloss: head turned back over the shoulder, looking behind

dimensions.scale_citation: Expression descriptors as used in performance direction, restricted to states readable from a single frame.
dimensions.description: The emotional register the face is playing.

values.definition: Contained reaction; brow and mouth engaged, composure held.
Loss of composure; brow raised, mouth open, eyes rolled or shut. Corresponds to the folksonomy term rendered as 'ahegao' in anime-domain tagging.

values.policy_note: Nonconsent-coded when combined with an explicit act. Enumerated so it can be excluded by rule; consumers operating a consent-forward posture should reject this value in combination with any explicit primary_act.

dimensions.scale_citation: Discrete mouth configurations readable from a single frame.
dimensions.description: The configuration of the mouth, recorded separately from affect because it is independently controllable and frequently mis-rendered.

aggregation_notes.note: Recorded per participant. A two-participant record carries two expression sets.

references: Danbooru tag group: face tags and expression folksonomy, consulted for coverage of readable expression states; wording original.
Gaze/affect/mouth three-way split is original to this vocabulary; consulted folksonomies bundle these into single tags.
